To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pointing error effect is more important than the turbulence's effect at the systems' outage capacity.
The outage capacity is a function of the pointing errors, the atmospheric turbulence strength, the link length, the transmitted power and the receiver's aperture diameter.

the outage capacity of FSO links over gamma turbulence channels with pointing error, is reduced significantly as compared to the outage capacity of the same links over gamma turbulence channel without pointing error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the outage capacity of FSO systems, over gamma modeled channels, with pointing errors.
the estimation of the outage capacity of FSO systems, over gamma turbulence channels with pointing error.
the investigation of FSO systems' performance over weak gamma turbulence channels with pointing error effects and the estimation of their capacity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pointing errors have a significant impact at the systems' capacity and the outage capacity estimation is a very effective metric for the systems' performance analysis, especially in the presence of the atmospheric turbulence.

the pointing errors effect is more significant for weak turbulence conditions, where the gamma distribution model is more accurate, and for low values of the pointing errors standard deviation, where their effect is more pronounced.
the outage capacity decreases with the increase of the turbulence strength, while the pointing errors effect is not so significant, as the outage capacity is almost unaffected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pointing errors have a significant impact on the systems' performance.
the pointing error effect is very significant and the systems' performance decreases rapidly with its increase, especially at low signal to noise ratio (SNR) values.
the outage capacity of FSO systems over gamma turbulence channels with pointing error effects, is significantly reduced compared to the case of the absence of turbulence and/or pointing errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pointing errors effect can be considered as an additional source of fading and thus, it should be taken into consideration in order to estimate accurately the systems' performance.

pointing errors and the gamma distribution, which is a very accurate statistical model for weak atmospheric turbulence conditions, should be taken into consideration in order to obtain a more accurate performance estimation of FSO systems.
the pointing errors effect is more significant than the atmospheric turbulence effect.
